digest_title: ShadowContext Security Digest: Fail-Closed Boundaries and Authorization
dek: Defensive analysis of critical vulnerabilities in MemOS, Ray, OpenSSL, Forminator, and GitLab requiring upgrades and fail-closed validation.
overview: Recent vulnerability disclosures highlight critical risks in AI memory, developer tooling, cryptographic fallbacks, and content management systems. Organizations must prioritize upgrades, enforce strict authentication, and validate fail-closed controls across all exposed boundaries.

stories.headline: MemOS Authentication Bypass Requires Fail-Closed Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-75110 in MemOS allows omitted environment values for internal secrets to grant administrative access without API keys.
stories.why_it_matters: Omitted identity signals must never equal successful matches on elevated service paths.

stories.headline: Ray Exploitation Demands Browser-Resistant Boundaries
stories.summary: CISA added CVE-2025-62593 to its catalog, highlighting DNS rebinding risks where browser heuristics fail to secure Ray dashboards.
stories.why_it_matters: Address scope and request headers are weak substitutes for positive identity checks.

stories.headline: Cryptographic Fallbacks Demand Fail-Closed Testing
stories.summary: CVE-2026-74900 and CVE-2026-74901 show silent cryptographic fallbacks in opensslencrypt allowing weaker security modes upon failure.
stories.why_it_matters: Failed cryptographic prerequisites must always produce explicit failure instead of reduced protection.

stories.headline: Forminator Fixes Demand Upload Boundary Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-15748 in Forminator exposes unauthenticated arbitrary file upload risks through blocklist bypasses and MIME handling.
stories.why_it_matters: Servers must independently enforce upload policy and store files outside executable web paths.

stories.headline: GitLab Public Projects Need Mutation Boundaries
stories.summary: CVE-2026-19478 in GitLab allows unauthenticated users to modify or delete public projects through GraphQL directives.
stories.why_it_matters: Public visibility must not be treated as write authority for state-changing operations.

operating_view: Maintain rigorous asset inventories and verify that all controls enforce explicit failure states. Treat updates as initial steps and demand behavioral proof that security boundaries hold against unauthenticated and malformed inputs.
watch_items: Verify software bills of materials and runtime versions for open-source dependencies and plugins.
Test that all administrative and data endpoints fail closed when authentication tokens are missing.
Ensure public data visibility never bypasses object-level authorization for state changes.
